title: Cue the stay
note: The cue hand is flat and vertical, palm out at chest height — a stop sign, not the flat upturned palm that means payment in door-sound-04-treats. Two different hands mean two different things and they are three screens apart.
scene: Interior entry hall, side view, camera at standing eye level. This is the same room, the same camera position and the same distance from the viewer as the other rungs of this ladder: Lucy's rectangular cool-grey dog bed on the left, the closed charcoal front door on the right, and a clear span of taupe-grey floor between them, with the whole walk from bed to door visible in frame. Lucy lies on the bed in a settled down — elbows and hips on the bed, head up and level, watching calmly. Her size in frame, the bed's position and the camera never change between these pictures. No leash. The handler stands right beside the bed, close enough to touch it, turned toward Lucy. Her near hand is raised to chest height and held flat and VERTICAL — palm facing Lucy, fingers pointing up, like a stop sign. It is not palm-up and not held out to be sniffed. Her other arm hangs at her side. Lucy holds her down and meets the handler's eye, head up, ears attentive, without getting up. The front door stays closed across the room.
mustBeTrue: the handler's cue hand is flat and vertical with the palm facing Lucy at chest height, not palm-up and not lowered toward her, and Lucy stays lying down on the bed with her head up meeting the handler's eye.
